newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Gov seeks to cut 1,700 state workers - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Gov seeks to cut 1,700 state workers - paper.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki signed a bill that would let state workers retire early or transfer to other jobs if they are at risk of having their jobs cut, the Albany Times Union reported Thursday.
The bill, approved by the legislature last week, extends a program used last year to cut the state work force and minimize firings.

The paper said the governor wants to cut the number of state employees by 1,700 in the 1998 fiscal year. The reductions would be in addition to the 18,500 jobs he eliminated during his first two years as governor.
The early retirement incentive remains the same as last year's, as it is open to workers who are at least 50 years old and have at least 10 years of service.
Retirees will get a month of pension credit for every year of service, up to a 36-month maxium. But the plan is limited to workers whose jobs are targeted for being eliminated, the paper said.
